note: The reported symptom is literally 'doesn't compile with dxc' -- the issue never quotes a diagnostic, so exit status is the only thing the report actually asserts. Deliberately NOT a text match: cross-referenced #2191 says the closely-related scalar [numthreads] case *asserts*, and this ground truth is a Debug build, so the same defect could surface as a trapped assert here and as a clean 'error:' line in the shipping Release binaries used for bisection. A text predicate would score whichever of those it was not written against as 'fixed'. nonzero_exit covers both signatures and is positive rather than absence-based, so it cannot be satisfied for free by a compile that never started. Its weakness is the opposite one -- it would also fire on a failure unrelated to this issue -- which is why (a) the reporter's own inlined-constant version is captured as a negative control (variant-control-inlined-*.txt, --expect no-match) and (b) every bisection probe's captured output was read rather than trusted. Note that classify() only downgrades a probe to invalid-probe when it scores no-repro, so a positive predicate cannot self-detect an unsupported-feature rejection; reading the outputs is what covers that.
